4912.title: [skills] Close pr-commit-message gaps found in release reviews
4912.body:
[skills] Close pr-commit-message gaps found in release reviews (#4912)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4895
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4907
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4908
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4910

Turn corrections from five completed release-message reviews into durable
pr-commit-message rules, then replace conclusion-led evals with cases that
exercise those decisions. Keep #4908 as an unchanged reviewed-message control;
it is distinct from the synthetic compact-message eval fixture.

~~ Durable topic boundaries ~~

The #4889 draft distributed shared command-safety guarantees among consumer
sections and under-described the deleted release-status runtime. Treat a shared
guard, mechanism, or contract as its own topic when its consumers do not own
its guarantee. A removal remains with its parent topic, but must preserve the
departing component's name, the behavior that left, and its new home.

Name sections for the problem or decision rather than a component, lead the
overview with the governing design, and require sibling sections to carry
comparable evidence. This preserves both the shared safety contract corrected
in #4889 and the regression-coverage sentence restored to #4895.

~~ Immediate dependency relationships ~~

The #4907 and #4910 drafts labelled an earlier stack ancestor as required even
though each change built on a nearer parent. Define `Requires:` as the immediate
companion or dependency that must land first; earlier ancestors provide
`Context:` instead. Candidate references still have to be opened and classified
by their actual entity and relationship before they are included.

~~ Complete and current evidence scopes ~~

The #4889 review disproved "every workflow is one manual job" because the
sampled family also contained scheduled and CI-only workflows. Require a family
to be enumerated along the generalized dimension, and narrow a quantified claim
when any member is a counterexample.

State coverage in the predicates that tests or guards actually assert rather
than the broader capability they suggest. Re-read counts and measurements at
the current head so later pushes cannot leave a once-correct number in the
message; #4910's tracked-file and nightly figures both changed during review.

~~ Configuration and migration intent ~~

Add configuration or policy splits and removals to the change-specific content
rules. Each configuration must identify its context, value, and reason for
remaining different, while a migration must identify the removed component and
where its responsibility moved. This records #4910's build-feed versus
public-package boundary instead of inviting a future maintainer to unify the
sources and invalidate publication verification.

~~ Concrete guarantees and lasting rationale ~~

Replace safety adjectives with the operation that cannot occur and the
neighboring system it cannot affect. That distinction preserves #4895's marker
ownership and #4907's rule that release testing neither publishes packages nor
changes BAR state.

Keep durable limitations, but discard scope-negotiation phrases such as
"excluded by request" or "out of scope for review size". Those phrases describe
development chronology and stop being true when a follow-up lands, as the #4910
review demonstrated.

~~ Facts that share a role word ~~

Three drafts of this PR joined two true facts into a false relationship because
both objects were called a control. #4908 is the prior release-message review
that needed no correction; `control-single-topic-compact` is a synthetic eval
for an unrelated design-time-detection change.

Extend the mixed-truth check to distinguish objects called control, baseline,
fixture, or config before joining clauses about them. A rerun then kept the two
controls separate while preserving the other fifteen ground-truth checks.

~~ Source-backed, copy-ready attribution ~~

Two eval runs found output defects independent of message prose: one invented a
Copilot noreply trailer without evidence, and another placed a valid trailer
outside the fence where it would not be copied into the commit. Accept an email
only from relevant commit authors, co-author trailers, or a non-null user email;
house-style trailers are not evidence.

Put every verified trailer inside the fenced commit message after a blank line.
Only a missing-context notice for a contributing human whose email cannot be
verified remains outside the fence.

~~ Evals that discriminate judgement ~~

The original eval pass scored 33/35 for the revision and 32/35 for the baseline,
inside run-to-run noise. Its prompts supplied conclusions, numbered notes gave
away topic counts, and one assertion hard-coded a section count; both graders
identified the assertions as non-discriminating.

Replace those cases with seven raw-evidence scenarios containing the stale
claims that caused the real review corrections: a contradicted workflow
universal, the wrong stack dependency, an unsafe configuration unification,
stale measurements, shared guarantees, attribution evidence, and a compact
single-topic control.

The rebuilt suite scored 39/41 for the revised skill and 36/41 for the baseline,
with no case regressing and wins on immediate dependencies, shared-mechanism
placement, and concrete safety claims. The universal and coverage rules were
already handled by both configurations, so they remain defensive rules rather
than measured wins. Trailer-sensitive reruns passed every assertion after the
output-contract fixes.

4910.title: [infra] Align release ecosystem references with dnceng
4910.body:
[infra] Align release ecosystem references with dnceng (#4910)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4803
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4907
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/commit/086f728b32d3423dc234cbb3e5a0bbec083d1cfe
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/33565525986

Build on #4907's merged BAR-specific approval implementation with the current
dnceng observer and shared-feed model. Keep the shared channel destinations
for ordinary CI and nightly consumers distinct from the selected BAR asset's
GUID-backed per-build feed; NuGet.org remains a later team publication step.

The dnceng observer state and the versioning, shared.cake, and building-samples
feed URLs were extracted from #4889 before that merged PR dropped these paths.
The pinned commit above is that stack's last state before the drop; its tree
still holds those files at this revision, apart from three building-samples
naming lines refreshed here. Its own diff covers unrelated release-notes work.
The README, benchmark/perf, writing-docs, and repository release-framing
updates are new here.

~~ dnceng pipeline observers ~~

Since #4803 moved release builds to dnceng, the DevDiv Native -> Managed ->
Tests definitions no longer describe them and ci-status reported a chain that
no longer runs. Query the `mono-SkiaSharp` validation definition 345 in
`dnceng-public/public` alongside skiasharp-package 1642 and skiasharp-tests
1630 in `dnceng/internal`. The cascade model becomes Build -> Tests: because
1642 owns native and managed work in one run, treat a red Tests run as a
cascade only when the exact Build run it consumed also failed, rather than
inferring the relationship from position in a three-stage chain.

Query Component Governance from skiasharp-package alone because that combined
Build owns native and managed assets, signing, API Scan, and BAR registration.
Drop the now-meaningless `--pipeline native|managed|both` selector, reject an
explicit security-audit build whose definition is not 1642, and point report
examples and the viewer at the dnceng/internal CG registration and Build.
With #4889 removing release-status, route build-progress and chain-tracing
questions to ci-status, and package-readiness checks to a release-publish dry
run. Skill metadata, representative report validators, Python compilation, and
JSON/XML parsing passed. Build-cache dependency validation covered 4,800
tracked files with none uncovered.

  * `SkiaSharp-Tests` in `scripts/infra/tests/tests-apple.cake` remains a
    simulator instance name, not a stale pipeline reference.

~~ Shared channels and BAR-specific approval ~~

The old skiasharp-transport service index returns HTTP 404, while the
`aka.ms/skiasharp-eap` alias resolves to the old skiasharp feed and does not
expose current nightlies. Point wrapper downloads and documentation at
dotnet-libraries-transport, document both shared destinations in versioning,
and point README, benchmark, and size-tracking sources at dotnet-libraries.

The merged #4907 implementation asks Maestro which BAR produced the selected
version, then resolves that BAR asset's GUID-backed V3 and flat-container feed
through Darc. Its planner downloads SkiaSharp, SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz, and the
derived HarfBuzzSharp dependency from that exact feed, requires matching source
branch and commit, and pins the same feed in every runner command, with
dependencies from dotnet-public.

Keep #4907's integration root, project, and generated-config propagation
inherited from main and outside this PR's direct diff. In
`documentation/dev/releasing.md` record that Arcade routes `IsShipping=true`
packages to dotnet-libraries and `IsShipping=false` build inputs to
dotnet-libraries-transport, then draw the shared-channel versus per-build BAR
feed boundary.

Because #4907 merged only implementation and integration files, this layer
renders the complete operator flow in `documentation/dev/releasing.md`. It also
replaces the three stale public-smoke references in `AGENTS.md` and the
release skill descriptions in the AI index with pre-publication BAR package
approval guidance. The guide records that release-testing physically
smoke-tests the exact selected CI artifacts on the approved host/device targets
and excludes NuGet.org from planner and runner sources, while the AI index
explains that repository-owned workflows and PowerShell scripts perform release
mutations and the skills remain thin guidance and observation layers.

The release-testing contract inherited from #4907 governs the gate: failed
required coverage blocks human release approval, but release-testing never
publishes packages or changes BAR state, and only after approval does the team
publish the selected BAR to NuGet.org.

The live planner resolved SkiaSharp 4.150.3 through BAR 329644 to GUID feed
8bf0dc6d-5564-4f8e-8ff2-8167b63c6306 and matched all three anchors to source
commit f8a404ff3375872d042404a29189ceb8e3001a41. Both shared feed indexes
returned HTTP 200, all 38 Python tests and the guarded PowerShell suite passed,
and GUID-feed restore passed all three SmokeTests with HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1.3.

End-to-end transport validation also passed. Externals-download fetched 18
wrappers and produced 462 native files (3.2 GB); docs-download-output fetched
four wrappers and produced 41 NuGet packages (570 MB). The linked benchmark run
completed successfully with all 20 jobs passing on this exact head.

  * `scripts/infra/package/manage-nuget-feed.ps1` retains the dedicated
    skiasharp and skiasharp-transport destinations. It exists to migrate
    historical xamarin feeds and is run manually for that purpose; repointing
    it at shared feeds would change the migration's meaning.
  * #4907's checked-in fallback config retains the old skiasharp feed name, but
    approval runs override restore sources and generated configs with the
    resolved GUID feed. Those files are inherited from main and remain outside
    this PR.

4907.title: [release] Resolve BAR packages for release approval
4907.body:
[release] Resolve BAR packages for release approval (#4907)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889
Context: https://github.com/appium/appium-mac2-driver/pull/411

Make release testing the human approval gate between a completed Build/Tests
BAR and team publication. Bind the test plan to one immutable package family,
propagate its exact source through the platform matrix, and report approval
without publishing packages or changing BAR state.

~~ BAR package identity ~~

The previous planner depended on the removed release-status handoff and a
global preview feed. A package version is not enough to identify a release
candidate because multiple BARs can produce the same version on separate Darc
feeds.

Take the exact SkiaSharp package version and resolve its producing build with
`darc get-asset`. Require `--bar-id` when the result is ambiguous and reject
already released builds, incomplete source metadata, and BARs without exactly
one NuGet location. Resolve that location through its single
`PackageBaseAddress` resource to obtain the build-specific GUID feed.

Download SkiaSharp and SkiaSharp.HarfBuzz from that feed, derive the bridge's
one concrete HarfBuzzSharp dependency, and download it from the same source.
Require each archive to contain one nuspec with its exact ID, version, branch,
and 40-character commit. The three packages must agree on branch and commit,
and the SkiaSharp metadata must match the selected BAR. Typed Darc and NuGet
adapters isolate command, feed, and package parsing from matrix construction.

~~ Exact restore source ~~

Put the selected SkiaSharp version, HarfBuzzSharp version, and GUID feed in
every generated runner command. The integration project requires those values,
uses the BAR feed plus dotnet-public for restore, and passes the feed into the
test runtime. Generated console, Blazor, MAUI, and Linux Docker projects write
the same source pair instead of using the global EAP feed and NuGet.org.

This prevents another build's copy of the same package version from satisfying
a restore. Tests round-trip each planned command through its runner parser and
verify that the checked-in integration sources propagate the BAR feed to root
and generated projects.

~~ Approval workflow ~~

Keep pipeline and package responsibilities separate. The release owner first
confirms that Build and Tests succeeded and that Tests consumed the selected
Build resource; the planner then verifies BAR and package identity. The skill
requires approval of the exact host matrix before preparation, executes all
selected items while collecting independent failures, preserves artifacts and
retries, combines cross-host reports, and treats missing required coverage as
blocking unless the owner records an override.

Planning remains read-only. A guarded PowerShell preparation script restores
repository tools and clears only `output/logs/testlogs/integration` after
approval. Python remains the runner runtime so subprocess heartbeats, command
round-tripping, interrupts, and temporary-device cleanup share one testable
implementation. The planner emits only the release, host, matrix, missing
coverage, and package-source data consumed by the runbook. Release-tooling CI
now covers the skill scripts, preparation guard, and integration harness.

The workflow never queues release pipelines, publishes packages, changes BAR
state, creates tags or releases, or merges code.

~~ Automation compatibility and ownership ~~

Treat Appium and its platform drivers as minimum-version prerequisites rather
than exact pins, accepting stable compatible updates while rejecting missing,
older, and prerelease versions. Both prerequisite validation and the test
fixture invoke `npm exec --no -- appium` from the repository root. This follows
Appium's project-local and Extension CLI resolution rules without downloading
software or depending on an extension's filesystem path.

Mac2 4.1.1 is the minimum because upstream PR #411 added Xcode 27 support.
Remove the process-local Xcode 26 selection workaround while retaining the
generated MAUI build's workload-version override.

Without `--device-id`, Android creates a uniquely named release-owned AVD on
the next free supported emulator port, leaves existing devices untouched, and
deletes only that AVD. Explicit `--device-id` is the only reuse path and never
deletes the selected device. iOS continues to create a fresh simulator and
falls back to its unique name for cleanup when creation returns no UDID.

4908.title: Move release milestone maintenance to PowerShell
4908.body:
[release] Move milestone maintenance to PowerShell (#4908)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889

Replace the skill-local Python implementation with repository-owned PowerShell
entry points and a thin dispatch workflow. Keep release assignment
reconciliation separate from schedule advancement, and make both operations
read-only unless a maintainer explicitly supplies `-Push`.

~~ Shipped release assignments ~~

Release assignments need to follow the release where a change actually shipped,
rather than the first branch on which it was planned. The reconciler orders the
release branches for one numeric line, accepts only exact public tags as shipped
boundaries, and rolls an unshipped preview or RC forward to the next shipped
milestone.

It finds the most recent earlier stable tag, compares each shipped tag from its
merge base, and reads first-parent subjects ending in `(#N)`. GitHub closing
references and closing keywords in the pull request body add linked issues.
Missing tags, boundaries, or milestones remain warnings in a dry run and become
hard blockers with `-Push`, so incomplete release evidence cannot write
assignments.

Every mutation uses the shared guarded GitHub helper and is verified after a
push. A live read-only run for 4.151.0 identified #4480 for 4.151.0-rc.1 and
found 103 assignments already correct without changing GitHub state.

~~ Milestone schedule and closure ~~

Milestone dates need to stay aligned with Chromium while shipped milestones
must not close over unfinished work. The updater reads the repository major and
Skia milestone, maps the six Chromium schedule fields to preview.1, preview.2,
RC, and stable dates and descriptions, and maintains three milestone cycles by
default. Missing historical entries more than 30 days past due are not
recreated.

An open milestone is eligible for closure only when its exact release tag
exists. Open work moves to the next unshipped open or planned milestone; a
missing destination blocks closure. Push mode synchronizes milestone metadata
first, verifies each move, waits for the old milestone to empty, rejects newly
arrived items, then closes the milestone and verifies its final state.

The dispatch validates its selected operations, requires a version for
reconciliation, serializes milestone runs, and leaves push disabled by default.
The release-tooling gate parses every publishing script, validates entry-point
help, and runs 69 publishing plus 25 focused milestone checks. A live read-only
schedule run planned no creates, updates, or closures.

4889.title: [release] Move publishing automation to repository-owned PowerShell
4889.body:
[release] Move publishing automation to repository-owned PowerShell (#4889)

Requires: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4895
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4908

Replace the Python runtimes behind the release-branch, release-publish, and
release-status skills, together with the milestones issue-template updater, with
three repository-owned PowerShell entry points under scripts/infra/publishing.
Internal builds, tests, signing, BAR promotion, and NuGet.org publication stay
in the team-owned pipeline; the repository owns only branch preparation, public
GitHub finalization, and issue-form maintenance. The release-branch and
release-publish skills remain as guidance over the scripts, while release-status
and its pipeline-status.py runtime are deleted because pipeline monitoring
belongs to the team pipeline. Reviewed Release summaries, smoke testing,
milestone maintenance, and dnceng observer or feed alignment are deliberately
outside this layer.

~~ Release branch preparation ~~

Add Release - Prepare and prepare-release.ps1 around an explicit base and exact
preview, RC, stable, or hotfix identity. The base must carry the requested
three-part SkiaSharp version or the immediately preceding four-part hotfix; the
script requires SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp to move together, checks the pinned
externals/skia gitlink, and creates matching mono/SkiaSharp and mono/skia
branches. Existing remote branches are authoritative: a matching ref is reused
and a conflicting one stops the run. A dry run prints copyable commands, -Apply
creates local branches and commits, and -Push performs remote writes.

A three-part stable cut changes only the release label, then opens a reviewable
pull request on a bump-version branch named for the next SkiaSharp patch, moving
the selected maintenance line to that patch and the next HarfBuzzSharp revision
at preview.0. That PR targets an existing, manually created release/X.Y.x
servicing branch when present; otherwise it targets main. Preparation never
creates the optional servicing branch. A four-part hotfix must advance the base
by exactly one revision and increments HarfBuzzSharp with it.

A rare hotfix from an older base can reuse a HarfBuzzSharp revision that a newer
line already published because allocation is relative to the selected base, not
global publication history. Maintainers must check that case manually; a global
allocator was deliberately deferred.

~~ Public release finalization ~~

Add Release - Finish and finish-release.ps1 for packages already public on
NuGet.org. An abbreviated preview or RC identity is accepted only when it
resolves to one public SkiaSharp package version. The script reads the source
branch and commit from that exact nuspec, warns when the recorded branch and
version identity disagree, and uses the recorded commit as the authority. It
creates or verifies the immutable exact-version tag and publishes a normal
GitHub-generated Release in one -Push run. A matching draft is published rather
than replaced; an already published Release is accepted by tag and prerelease
identity.

After publication, Finish dispatches release-note generation for that version;
stable releases also dispatch the issue-template update with push enabled.
Package publication, pipeline monitoring, draft-body formatting, and summary
ownership leave this layer. PR #4895 owns reviewed Release summaries, while
milestone maintenance and optional smoke testing remain focused upper layers.

~~ Issue-template version maintenance ~~

Port update-bug-template.py to update-bug-template.ps1 and simplify Sync - Issue
Template Versions around it. Rebuild the version and goodversion dropdowns from
published, non-draft GitHub Releases while preserving unrelated YAML. Read-only,
local -Apply, and automation-branch -Push modes are supported. Scheduled daily
runs push, maintain one owned pull request, reuse identical branch content, and
refresh an existing automation branch only with an explicit force-with-lease.
Removing the old milestones directory also moves its cache input to
scripts/infra/publishing.

~~ Shared command safety and regression tests ~~

Route Git and GitHub execution through Git.Common.psm1, GitHub.Common.psm1, and
Publishing.Common.psm1 so production entry points do not invoke git or gh
directly. The modules run Git from an explicit repository root, retry transient
GitHub reads three times with backoff, print skipped mutations as copyable
commands that name their -Push guard, and verify relevant remote state after
writes.

Release - Tooling Tests runs the PowerShell harness on pull requests, main
pushes, and manual dispatch. The mutating workflows require the default branch,
keep mutation inputs false by default, and reject simultaneous -Apply and -Push
where both modes exist. Tests cover mode isolation, direct git and gh invocation
guards, package/version transforms, hotfix progression, guarded branch pushes,
release identity, issue-form rendering, force-with-lease usage, and
automation-branch reuse.

4895.title: [release] Split reviewed GitHub Release summaries
4895.body:
[release] Add reviewed GitHub Release summaries (#4895)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4889

Add an exact-shipment layer to release-note generation so reviewed prose can
converge on each tagged GitHub Release without delaying publication or requiring
publishing automation to prepare body markers. Keep Markdown structure, links,
contributor credit, marker ownership, and writes deterministic; the
release-notes agent supplies only short reviewed prose.

~~ Exact shipment facts ~~

Bump release data to format 4 and record one shipment for every strict
preview, RC, stable, or hotfix tag whose core version matches a released page.
Derive the core/public versions, channel, label, target commit, date, previous
tag in global release order, exact compare URL, and PR delta from repository
facts. Ignore decorative legacy tags instead of classifying them, fail loudly
on inconsistent committed data, and accept two-part Arcade prerelease build
revisions such as `-rc.1.26426.14` alongside single-part revisions. The
generator now requires Python 3.10 or later.

Broad convergence skips data from older formats, while an explicit request for
one of those tags fails with regeneration guidance.

Split strict data equality from website-content equality. Shipment-only
additions, removals, and changes now rewrite `data.json` without discarding
reviewed website prose or requesting another polish pass. Website-facing fact
changes still invalidate prose, while `--force` requests polish without
discarding prose for fully unchanged pages. This prevents a new tag from being
skipped when its shipment is the only changed fact.

Regression coverage exercises exact tag ordering, tag-derived metadata and
changelog endpoints, falsey non-array rejection, and shipment-only writes.

~~ Reviewed prose and deterministic rendering ~~

Add optional `release_summaries` prose keyed by exact shipment tag. An omitted
entry remains ineligible until its reviewed headline and optional body are
ready, allowing tags to converge independently. Point the release-notes skill
and the `update-release-notes` agentic workflow at the new slot, with the
downstream updater rather than the website renderer owning its safety checks
and application; regenerate the compiled lock file to match.

Render the shipment label, vetted contributor handles, and deterministic NuGet,
website release-notes, and exact changelog links outside agent-authored prose.
Reject code fences, managed sentinels, raw HTML comments, security claims,
placeholders, structural openers, unknown fields, and overlong prose before a
release write can begin. Drop contributor logins that are not syntactically
valid GitHub handles from the credits line. Regression coverage exercises each
rejection rule, login filtering, and deterministic link and credit rendering.

~~ Published Release convergence ~~

Add a classic workflow for scoped main pushes, published-release events, and
manual dispatches. Release and manual events read reviewed facts from trusted
`main`; the workflow does not create, tag, or publish releases.

Own the four body markers and a minimal GitHub REST client in Python, with no
`gh` CLI dependency. The first reviewed update adopts an unmarked published
Release by wrapping and preserving its existing GitHub-generated body; later
updates replace only the managed summary region. This lets publishing create an
ordinary GitHub-generated Release without sharing the marker contract. Missing
releases and unpublished drafts are skipped, and an already-current body is
left untouched.

Preflight the full candidate batch, then re-read every planned body before the
first PATCH because the REST API offers no conditional body update. Abort
before any write when validation fails or a concurrent edit is detected, and
re-read each updated Release to require the stored body to match exactly.
Regression coverage exercises adoption, generated-body preservation, draft
convergence, idempotence, race detection, unsafe-batch rejection, and failed
write verification.

Document the format-4 shipments field, package layout, and updater preflight,
race-barrier, and verification flow in the release-notes development guide.

4884.title: Update .NET SDK and container pins to 10.0.400
4884.body:
Update .NET SDK and container pins to 10.0.400 (#4884)

Context: https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.11/10.0.11.md
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4842
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1572959

Adopt the .NET 10.0.11 security servicing release while preserving the
toolchain exceptions established by #4842 for WinUI and Apple workloads.
10.0.11 shipped SDKs 10.0.400, 10.0.303, and 10.0.111; it shipped no 10.0.2xx
SDK, and that band last shipped 10.0.204 in 10.0.8.

~~ Repository SDK alignment ~~

Move `global.json`, its `tools.dotnet` selector, and the central
`DOTNET_VERSION` from 10.0.203 to SDK 10.0.400. Keep `latestPatch`
roll-forward so resolution stays inside the selected feature band.

Raise the integration-test and release-test SDK default from 10.0.100 to
10.0.400. Those harnesses generate temporary projects outside the checkout
and write their own `global.json`, so they do not inherit the root pin. They
retain `latestFeature` roll-forward and now require at least the repository's
feature band instead of accepting any .NET 10 feature band.

~~ Repository-bound and consumer container roles ~~

Update the docs image, native Android, Linux, Tizen, and WASM SDK installs,
CI container-test images, and `tests/Dockerfile.linux` to 10.0.400. Preserve
the existing distro and OS suffixes: `-noble`, `-alpine3.23`,
`-azurelinux3.0`, and `-nanoserver-ltsc2022`.

Keep the isolated sample images and generated Linux package-consumer test on
floating `10.0` tags. Their build contexts exclude the root `global.json`, so

4803.title: Migrate CI to dnceng with Arcade shipping and transport
4803.body:
Migrate CI to dnceng with Arcade shipping and transport (#4803)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4775
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4800
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4801
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4802
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4838
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4842
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4846
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4859
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-SkiaSharp/pullrequest/63954
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build/results?buildId=3057398

Replace the legacy DevDiv Native -> Managed -> Tests chain with repository-owned
dnceng pipelines and a standard Arcade V3 package flow. Keep public validation
unsigned, reserve protected identities for internal signing, scanning, BAR
registration, and promotion, and leave the binding, native, and runtime product
surface unchanged.

~~ Connected dnceng topology ~~

The split Native and Package definitions handed artifacts across independently
numbered runs, which made source, package, and test provenance harder to keep
connected. Make internal definition 1642 own Prepare, Native, and Package in one
Build run, and make Tests 1630 consume the folder-qualified
`\dotnet\skiasharp\skiasharp-package` resource. Trigger 1642 directly for
`main` and `release/*` path changes, plus a daily main schedule, instead of
waiting for completion of a separate Native pipeline.

Remove the obsolete native-only and internal-complete YAML roots, and derive
managed, test, and sample dependencies from the shared build/test pipeline role.
Public definition 345 and downstream Tests 1630 keep those shared stages through
the local output adapter; for public CI this avoids the inaccessible private 1ES
template repository. Expansion guards require the internal project, a non-PR
reason, and a non-PR ref before signing, compliance, or publishing stages can
exist.

~~ dnceng execution policy ~~

Move the internal root from the DevDiv MicroBuild 1ES template to the released
v1 1ES Official template, and move its Windows and Linux agents to
NetCore1ESPool-Internal. Apple jobs remain on Microsoft-hosted macOS images.
Armory, BinSkim, CredScan, ESLint, PoliCheck, and PSScriptAnalyzer are
configured to break; CodeQL also runs on non-default branches. Network
isolation remains in Audit while permanent mirrors and allowlisting are
completed.

The combined root carries forward the managed Apple macOS 15/Xcode 26.3 and
native Apple macOS 14/Xcode 16.2 split. The repository remains on SDK 10.0.203
and workload set 10.0.202, but Visual Studio MSBuild 17.x cannot load .NET
10.0.2xx. Install `DOTNET_VERSION_WINUI` (10.0.108) side by side on the three
WinUI C++/WinRT jobs. Build and merge the MSVC Win32 artifacts unconditionally,
dropping the former `System.TeamProject == 'devdiv'` gate.

~~ Provider-neutral build identity ~~

Replace feature-name and loosely parsed downstream counters with Arcade's
`yyyyMMdd.revision` OfficialBuildId, converted to the existing
`short-date.revision` package suffix. Normalize GitHub and Azure Repos PR
numbers, source commits, source branches, and repository URLs before packing;
fail when required identity is absent or an inherited Build run name is
malformed.

PR builds use `pr.<number>`, scheduled builds use `nightly`, and ordinary builds
retain their source-controlled label. A producing pipeline may select the
`stable` sentinel only on an internal `release/*` branch; it clears the suffix
to produce exact `X.Y.Z` packages. Downstream Tests inherit the selected Build
run name, including an exact-release identity, rather than generating a second
identity.

Each run creates one transport alias family as well: PR aliases for PR
validation and branch aliases otherwise. Remove commit aliases so one BAR cannot
receive multiple versions of the same transport package ID. Package outputs are
not cached because their versions and transport family depend on run identity,
not only repository inputs.

~~ Deterministic Arcade package inputs ~~

Replace the separate normal and special packaging jobs, and the stable, preview,
and symbol transport variants they produced, with one Cake graph in a single
`package_windows` job. It publishes raw `nuget` and `nuget_special` artifacts
plus prepared `arcade_shipping`, `arcade_nonshipping`, and `PdbArtifacts`
inputs. Shipping contains product and explicit symbol packages; NonShipping
contains the run's single `_NuGets`/`_NativeAssets*` transport family.
`_NuGets` uses numbered dependency packages to keep each payload chunk near
200 MB.

Arcade V3 expects `PdbArtifacts`, so provide real loose symbols rather than a
permanent placeholder or manufactured fallback packages. For product packages
without an explicit symbol package, extract implementation and runtime PDBs
under package/version/TFM/RID paths. Exclude `ref/**`, reject ZIP paths that
escape the package root, avoid loose-PDB duplication for packages with explicit
symbols, and emit `.empty` only when no eligible PDB exists. Consume the Apple
symbol packages introduced by #4846 instead of manufacturing fallback copies.

The public PR downloaders now query definition 345 by exact PR merge ref,
consume the canonical `nuget` artifact, exclude `.symbols.nupkg`, and use
isolated temp directories. Documentation and sample generation select the
single package family instead of assuming stable and preview packages coexist.

The exact 3057398 artifact audit matched raw and prepared package payloads,
contained 209 path-safe loose PDBs, and confirmed that the Package stage emitted
only the five contract artifacts, with no `package_windows` artifact.

~~ Self-verifying build logic ~~

Build identity, API Scan input preparation, and Arcade asset assembly encode
release constraints that would otherwise fail only in later or protected
stages. Add dedicated suites for each and run them as pipeline gates rather than
relying on YAML string checks or post-release inspection.

Prepare runs `SetBuildVariables.Tests.ps1` and
`PrepareApiScanInputs.Tests.ps1` before product stages, so identity failures and
API Scan input drift are caught even when API Scan does not expand. Package runs
`AssembleArcadeAssets.Tests.ps1` after packing against real ZIP fixtures,
proving PDB extraction, `ref/**` exclusion, traversal rejection,
explicit-symbol ownership, PR/branch transport selection, and `.empty` fallback
on each run.

~~ Shipping-only signing ~~

Replace the legacy SignList and Arcade defaults with the explicit policy in
`eng/Signing.props`. Any new signable payload must be added to one of its
first-party, Mac developer, third-party, or skipped classifications for signing
validation to succeed. First-party binaries use the repository's certificate
mappings and skip the third-party copyright check because they intentionally
lack Microsoft copyright metadata.

Only prepared Shipping NuGets enter Arcade signing; product and explicit symbol
packages are signed together. `eng/SignCheckExclusionsFile.txt` marks
NonShipping transport `DO-NOT-SIGN, DO-NOT-UNPACK` and marks JavaScript and
generated WebGPU payloads `DO-NOT-SIGN`; those payloads use
`CertificateName=None` and remain authenticated by their signed NuGet container.
`DO-NOT-SIGN` is fail-closed, so SignCheck fails if a listed file is ever
signed.

Main and release branches select real signing automatically. Other trusted
internal branches test-sign unless `forceRealSigning` is requested, and forced
BAR side effects additionally require `registerInBar`. Use standard Arcade
SignTool and SignCheck validation rather than retaining the migration
prototype's duplicate recursive verifier.

~~ API Scan input coverage ~~

Move API Scan into a repository-owned internal stage that downloads the current
`nuget` and `native_msvc` artifacts, authenticates through the dedicated WIF
connection, and runs in release mode. Package extraction preserves symbols and
builds checked surrogates for Win32, NanoServer, and WinUI, including shipped
ARM64 binaries that require API-compatible x64 MSVC inputs. Use the same HTTPS
SymWeb symbol path in the scan task and generated surrogate configuration.

Input preparation fails when packages, binaries, PDBs, surrogate files, or
configured target matches are absent. Reporting, TSA upload, and PostAnalysis
use Note-level API Scan policy; raw logs are published for audit. The stage runs
when explicitly requested and on scheduled main builds, independently of BAR
registration.

~~ BAR registration and promotion ~~

Generate one Arcade V3 manifest from signed Shipping and prepared NonShipping
artifacts, with explicit symbol blobs and the standard PDB artifact alongside
it. Protected registration is structurally limited to non-PR internal builds.
Main and release branches register automatically; a forced feature-branch run
must opt into both real signing and BAR registration.

Use standard post-build validation with `publishAssetsImmediately: false` and
`requireDefaultChannels: true`, so a missing Maestro mapping fails closed and
Darc performs configured channel promotion only after asset publication
finishes. NuGet.org publication remains a separate protected operation; #4859
carries the release-tooling adaptation to this BAR model.

Exact Build 3057398 completed real signing, Note-level API Scan, BAR
registration, asset validation, and Darc promotion. BAR 328638 reached General
Testing with 41 shipping package assets, 22 non-shipping transport assets, 14
symbol blobs, and one manifest, with no recorded incoherencies or staleness.

4846.title: Generate Apple native symbol packages during pack
4846.body:
Generate Apple native symbol packages during pack (#4846)

Context: https://github.com/NuGet/Home/issues/15056
Context: https://github.com/NuGet/Home/issues/10860
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1565520

Generate native `.symbols.nupkg` outputs for the SkiaSharp and
HarfBuzzSharp Apple packages from the normal Cake/NuGet graph. Keep the
customer packages symbol-free and preserve their identity, metadata, and
runtime payload without reopening or modifying completed archives.

~~ Exact symbol-only pack content ~~

NuGet's supported `TfmSpecificDebugSymbolsFile` path filters symbol files
by source extension. Apple's framework dSYMs instead contain extensionless
`Contents/Resources/DWARF/<module>` files, and staging them with a
`.dwarf` extension changes the final package path. Ordinary `Pack=true`
content also enters the customer package, while `IncludeSource` forces
content under `src/`.

Introduce a generic `PackageSymbolFile` item and process it through a
guarded second invocation of the same project's ordinary `Pack` target.
The outer pack writes the customer package normally, then invokes an
isolated `NoBuild` pack with `PackNativeSymbols=true`. The inner pack maps
only `PackageSymbolFile` items to `None Pack=true` with their exact
`PackagePath`, after which the result is moved to the standard
`.symbols.nupkg` name. The recursion guard and isolated intermediate
directory keep the workaround deterministic while retaining NuGet's
normal package construction and metadata handling.

~~ Apple dSYM and Catalyst payloads ~~

Declare symbol content for the SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp native-assets
projects on macOS, iOS, Mac Catalyst, and tvOS. The packages carry the
complete arm64 and x86_64 dSYM bundles for each shipped device or simulator
runtime while leaving the existing customer `PackageFile` declarations
unchanged.

Mac Catalyst continues to ship its symlink-preserving `framework.zip`.
Because the symbol uploader does not recurse into that archive, its symbol
package also exposes the real
`<library>.framework/Versions/A/<library>` Mach-O alongside the dSYMs.

Build 1565520 emitted eight stable and eight preview Apple symbol packages.
Inspection of every pair confirmed matching package metadata, byte-identical
customer runtime payloads, no dSYM content in customer packages, official
extensionless DWARF names, complete dSYM trees, and real Catalyst versioned
modules.

~~ Deterministic package output cleanup ~~

Clear existing `.nupkg` and `.snupkg` files before the complete stable and
preview repack, and clear both formats from the symbol destination before
moving new symbol packages. This prevents an artifact left by another
version or platform build from surviving missing wildcard inputs and being
published as part of the current package set.

4815.title: [performance] Build Android on Linux and reduce CI overhead
4815.body:
[performance] Build Android on Linux and reduce CI overhead (#4815)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4816
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4818
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1557164
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1559377
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1559994
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1560012
Context: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_build/results?buildId=15017102
Context: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_build/results?buildId=15030082
Context: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_build/results?buildId=15032120
Context: https://dev.azure.com/devdiv/DevDiv/_build/results?buildId=15032942

Move Android native production to four Linux-container jobs, make native
bootstrap setup match the work each job performs, and stop special-package
creation from rebuilding managed outputs. The final cache-disabled public run
completed in 3h30m15s instead of 6h17m44s for cold main; raw agent usage fell
from 3,087.2 to 1,562.4 minutes. Main receives additional policy-injected work,
so those are end-to-end operational figures; the direct task and topology
measurements below are the causal evidence.

The final public run succeeded end to end. DevDiv native and package/signing
runs also succeeded. Its test run passed managed builds, samples, and every test
job except a macOS tests-netcore job canceled at 180 minutes without a product
or test error. Exact-main DevDiv and the automatic public PR run reproduced the
same timeout, while the cache-disabled final run passed macOS tests, so the hang
was accepted as pre-existing and non-blocking.

~~ Native bootstrap and checkout ~~

Container-native jobs installed Python, Ninja, and .NET on the host even though
the toolchain and Cake invocation run inside the image. Native source jobs also
initialized every submodule, while merge-only jobs fetched source they never
used and configured build variables a second time on cache misses.

Skip host Ninja and .NET for Docker-native jobs, retain Python whenever direct
execution or cache-key computation needs it, and preserve every direct
Windows/macOS prerequisite. Source jobs now initialize only Skia and
depot_tools; merge jobs initialize no submodules; build variables are configured
once. The new controls default to the old managed-job behavior.

Across the paired runs, full recursive submodule checkouts fell from 65 to zero,
replaced by 56 targeted native checkouts. Python selection fell from 88 to 38,
Ninja installation from 61 to 15, and .NET installation from 85 to 39, while the
119 required artifact downloads were preserved.

~~ Android native production ~~

The four Android ABIs were built on Windows and duplicated on macOS even though
native merge consumed only the Windows artifacts. Enable the existing Android
Cake targets on Linux, build x86, x64, arm, and arm64 in four parallel Docker
jobs, remove both host matrices, and make the Linux artifacts canonical merge
inputs.

The image tracks Microsoft's Azure Linux Android prerequisite tag, verifies
NDK r27c (27.2.12479018) and Ninja, and installs .NET SDK 10.0.108 with
the repository's standard dotnet-install script because the prerequisite image
does not contain the SDK. Startup diagnostics record the NDK path, CPU count,
and Ninja version. The moving base tag is not part of the output-cache key, so
a remote tag update is consumed only after a cache miss, cache-disabled run, or
tracked input change; it is deliberately not pinned by digest.

This replaces eight host jobs with four Linux jobs. In the paired cold runs,
Android agent usage fell from 429.9 to 61.6 minutes and the critical job from
1h14m10s to 15m34s. Across all four ABIs, both native libraries retained the
four-file .so/.dbg inventory, matching ELF machines, exported dynamic symbols,
DT_NEEDED sets, GNU debug links, and 0x4000 LOAD alignment.

~~ Special-package work ~~

nuget-special creates internal wrapper packages from existing native, normal
NuGet, and symbol outputs, but its root target depended on libs and rebuilt the
managed graph. Its separate job also installed Node, Android SDK/JDK, workloads,
and every submodule even though none participates in wrapper creation.

Remove the libs dependency while keeping normal and special packaging as

4694.body:
[release] Make release workflows deterministic and resumable (#4694)

Context: https://github.com/appium/appium-mac2-driver/issues/410

Define five script-backed release stages that carry one exact release identity
through branch creation, CI status, package testing, publication, and milestone
maintenance. Remote writes are driven by reviewable plans and pinned execution
commands, and reruns reconcile the exact approved state. This changes release
tooling, integration tests, and documentation only; it does not change public
APIs or runtime behavior.

~~ Pin release branches and CI handoffs ~~

Read version inputs from explicit refs and plan paired SkiaSharp and mono/skia
release branches from an exact base SHA and gitlink. Revalidate both identities
before creating refs, reconcile partially completed paired-branch creation, and
create a maintainer-owned version-bump PR after a stable cut.

Resolve one connected Native -> Managed -> Tests chain for the pinned commit.
Treat the newest Native attempt as authoritative and require downstream runs to
descend from it. Derive paired test and public versions from the selected
Managed build, verify both exact test packages on the preview feed, and preserve
the commit, run IDs, and versions in every downstream handoff. Twenty-five
branch scenarios and eleven status tests cover drift, partial state, hotfixes,
stable bump PRs, retry selection, and package readiness.

~~ Test the exact build across the release matrix ~~

Require explicit SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp package versions in the integration
project. Stable testing uses the produced X.Y.Z-stable.B packages while the bare
X.Y.Z versions remain separate publication state.

Plan smoke, console, Linux, Blazor, Android 26 and 37.1, Mac Catalyst, iOS 18.6
and 26.5, and Windows coverage as each host permits. Platform runners restore
pinned tools, validate exact runtimes and device ownership, clean up
release-owned devices, emit heartbeat progress, collect the complete initial
result set, and retry only after a concrete repair. Mac2 4.0.5 uses an installed
Xcode 26 process-locally until the pinned driver includes its Xcode 27 fix.
Passing tests remain the default publication gate, with an explicit
release-manager override available.

Thirty-four runner and planner tests pass. The integration smoke suite restored
SkiaSharp 4.152.0-preview.1.1 and HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1-preview.1.1, then passed
all three smoke tests.

~~ Resume publication across approvals and indexing ~~

Queue Azure pipeline 25298 with the exact Managed build number and validate its
resolved resource, destination, and push parameters. Interactive operation
returns the protected approval URL immediately; automation may wait for the
same run. Recovery detects exact queued, running, succeeded, or partially
indexed publication state without queueing a duplicate, and every resume command
pins the approved run ID.

Represent delayed NuGet.org indexing as a resumable wait-for-nuget state that
names each missing package. Keep immutable tag and generated-notes draft
creation separate from teaser review and final publication. Repository-specific
ordering selects the previous release across preview, RC, stable, and four-part
hotfix tags. Twenty-eight publication tests cover request identity, recovery,
tag ordering, draft safety, and delayed indexing.

~~ Reconcile shipped work and advance milestones ~~

Reconcile merged PRs and linked issues to their shipped release using
first-parent release boundaries and exact tags. Advance a default horizon of
three Skia milestones from Chromium dates, move open issues and pull requests
from tagged milestones to the next unshipped milestone, and close the shipped
milestone only after its approved moves are visible.

Use GitHub's REST issues endpoint so milestone rollover includes both issues and
pull requests. Poll for the approved item set to settle, tolerate normal
propagation delay, and block closure if a new item appears. Twenty-three tests
cover tag matching, assignment ranges, issue and PR rollover, future targets,
propagation, and closure ordering.

3969.title: Make the SkiaSharp canvas visible to Appium on Windows
3969.body:
MAUI's AutomationId maps to AutomationProperties.AutomationId on WinUI, which
is not enough to place an element in the UIA control view: TextBlock and
ApplicationBar appear because they are control elements, but the canvas is a
bare panel and was omitted, leaving the page content area childless. Appium
could therefore never find the canvas on Windows.

Setting SemanticProperties.Description maps to AutomationProperties.Name, which
gives the canvas a NamedContainerAutomationPeer and places it in the tree with
correct bounds, already expressed in the same pixels as the screenshot:

  SkiaCanvas Name='SkiaCanvas' Class='NamedContainerAutomationPeer' [462,273 500x375]

The existing accessibility id lookup then works unchanged, so Windows needs no
platform-specific code. Android and iOS are unaffected: Android locates the
canvas by resource id and iOS by accessibilityIdentifier, neither of which is
altered by adding a description.

Appium also could not be started on Windows: it is installed as appium.cmd,
which Process.Start cannot execute directly with UseShellExecute=false, so the
fixture threw before any test ran. Launch it through the platform shell and kill
the whole process tree on teardown, otherwise the server outlives its shell
wrapper and keeps holding port 4723.

SKTypeface.Default is Segoe UI here, and the glyph advances differ enough from
the shared reference to cost ~2% on their own. Like the iOS and Mac Catalyst

4670.body:
[skia-sync] Fix no-work detection after branch deletion (#4670)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/actions/runs/30963914803

When a merged `skia-sync/m<N>` branch had been deleted, the upstream
no-work detector only fell back to the resolved mono/skia base for
release destinations. A same-milestone request targeting SkiaSharp
`main` therefore had no comparison ref, reached EOF without emitting
a `skip` output, and activated the agent even though the upstream head
was already contained in `skiasharp`.

Check an existing sync branch first and otherwise compare against the
resolved mono/skia base for both `main` and release destinations. Use
GitHub's ancestry comparison to emit `skip=true` when the upstream head
is already contained and `skip=false` explicitly when work remains. A
new milestone naturally runs because its upstream head is not yet
contained in `skiasharp`.

Require an explicit `skip=false` before activating the agent, so a
missing output cannot be interpreted as work. If the compare API fails,
preserve the `gh` diagnostic, emit an actionable `::error::` naming the
upstream ref and SHA plus the mono/skia comparison ref, and exit
nonzero without emitting a skip decision.

Add eight deterministic cases covering same-milestone main no-op and
new-work states, existing sync branch precedence, release no-op, a
true milestone bump, explicit `skip=false`, and compare API failure.
Update the Skia workflow guidance to require ancestry rather than SHA
equality and regenerate the compiled workflow.

A live read-only M152 check resolved `chrome/m152` at `2a9b593bab4b`,
confirmed that it was contained in `skiasharp`, and emitted

4355.title: [memory-leak] Fix native use-after-free in SKRegion.SpanIterator (root the SKRegion)
4355.body:
[memory-leak] Root SKRegion for iterator lifetimes (#4355)

Context: #4354

SKRegion iterators hold native iterator state that references the source
region's run data. Because SKRegion skips global handle registration, the
region could be finalized while a SpanIterator was still alive, leaving the
native iterator with a dangling pointer and causing use-after-free.

Use SKObject.Referenced(this, region) for RectIterator, ClipIterator, and
SpanIterator so each iterator keeps its source region alive for its entire
lifetime. Add a regression test that forces collection and verifies the
SpanIterator remains usable. This keeps the iterator family consistent,
clears the keep-alive reference during disposal, and does not change the
public API or ABI.

Fixes #4354

4630.title: [performance] Cache HandleDictionary skip-registration reflection check
4630.body:

Context: #4629

wrap, but each call repeatedly used Type.IsAssignableFrom to determine whether the
wrapper type skips global registration. That predicate is invariant for each closed

hot path reads a plain static boolean. This preserves behavior and does not change
the public API or ABI.

Add parity tests covering skip-registration and tracked wrapper types, plus an
end-to-end deduplication check. Add a four-way benchmark comparing the existing
cached-Type baseline, inline typeof, the PR cache, and inline typeof inside the
generic cache. The generic cache variants are effectively equivalent; both avoid
the repeated reflection cost without allocations.

4605.title: [tests] Run ganesh-gl on the Windows and Linux CI legs
4605.body:
[tests] Run ganesh-gl on the Windows and Linux CI legs (#4605)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4605
Context: documentation/dev/gpu-test-policy.md
Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/4590

#4575 made a GPU backend required on every platform GpuPolicy.RequiredOn names
and turned the silent skips into an enumerable list. ganesh-gl was the largest
entry on it: required on Windows, macOS and Linux, but opted out of the two
desktop legs that had no working GL stack. This closes those, so the Ganesh GL
backend now runs on all three desktop platforms.

This is not "GL was untested until now". GL was already covered in several
places, and this fills in the ones that were not:

  * macOS already ran ganesh-gl through CGL. That is why ganesh-gl.macos was
    the only committed golden set — under the rules #4575 introduced, an
    unseeded backend fails, so those goldens exist because macOS was rendering.
  * Android, iOS and Mac Catalyst already exercise the views layer against real
    GL surfaces: MemoryLeakTests.SKGLViewHandlerDoesNotLeak runs and passes on
    all three device legs.
  * Windows had no OpenGL implementation at all, and Linux had GLX loading and
    then killing the host. Both are the low-level GRContext.CreateGl path the
    desktop console suite covers, and both are what this fixes.

The five container legs and Nano Server keep their opt-out, and the comment now
reads as a decision rather than a pending item: those images exist to prove
SkiaSharp works with the bare minimum installed, so giving them an X server and
Mesa would defeat their purpose.

Two gaps this does not close, both pre-existing: SKGLView on WinUI has no device
leg in this pipeline, and the Blazor SKGLView/WebGL test lives in
SkiaSharp.Tests.Integration, which this pipeline does not run. ganesh-gl is not
required on Browser at all; WASM's GPU backend is graphite-dawn, still opted out
because the headless browser exposes no adapter. #4591 tracks the remainder.

Every problem below was reproduced and measured before it was fixed: Mesa on
Windows, and Ubuntu under WSL with Xvfb and GLX for Linux, which reproduced the
CI crash faithfully enough to bisect it.

~~ Windows: no OpenGL at all ~~

The agents have no display driver carrying an OpenGL ICD, so opengl32.dll
answers with the in-box generic implementation: OpenGL 1.1, no
WGL_ARB_pixel_format, no WGL_ARB_pbuffer. WglContext cannot come up on that, and
Ganesh needs 3.0+ regardless.

scripts/infra/native/windows/install-mesa-gl.ps1 provisions Mesa the way Mesa
documents for machines with no OpenGL driver [0]: libgallium_wgl.dll becomes
System32\mesadrv.dll and SysWOW64\mesadrv.dll, registered under
OpenGLDrivers\MSOGL. It follows install-vulkan-icd.ps1 — pinned version, SHA-256
pin, both bitnesses, fatal on any failure — and checks what provisioning is
responsible for and no more: the driver is where opengl32 will look for it, its
version resource matches the version just pinned rather than a leftover from an
earlier run, and the registration reads back. Proving it renders belongs to the
suite, and GRContextTest.CreateDefaultContextIsValid already does that on every
leg where the policy requires ganesh-gl.

~~ Windows: SetPixelFormat and wglSetPixelFormat are not interchangeable ~~

With Mesa registered, provisioning still failed, and the diagnostics named it:

    mesadrv=C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\mesadrv.dll; pixelFormats=1332; chosenFormat=121
    FAILED: wglCreateContext returned NULL (2000)

Mesa is loaded and serving its own 1332 pixel formats, and 2000 is
ERROR_INVALID_PIXEL_FORMAT. gdi32's ChoosePixelFormat reports Mesa's formats and
SetPixelFormat returns true, but Mesa's per-HDC state is only created by its own
wglSetPixelFormat, so wglCreateContext has nothing to look up.

The two APIs turn out to be exactly inverted, consistently per driver: a
hardware ICD is set up through GDI and refuses a context when the format was set
the other way, and Mesa is the reverse. So the Wgl bootstrap tries GDI first —
every real driver, and every developer running these tests locally — and falls
back only when the context actually fails. A pixel format can be set once per
DC and the class is CS_OWNDC, so the retry needs a fresh window; the first is
destroyed before it is replaced.

~~ Linux: the crash was one test, not a race ~~

#4590 attributed the exit-7 host crash to nine test classes creating GLX
contexts concurrently. That diagnosis was wrong. The crash reproduces with the
suite serialized onto a single thread, and a trace shows every context created,
used and destroyed on that one thread.

The real cause is GRGlInterfaceTest.AssembleInterfaceIsValid, which resolved
Skia's proc addresses with glXGetProcAddress alone. Under GLVND — the
vendor-neutral libGL every current distro ships — that returns a dispatch stub
for any name at all; glTotallyNotARealFunction comes back non-null. Skia was
handed pointers that are not functions and walked off the end of the extension
list in GrGLExtensions::init. It now resolves through dlsym on libGL.so.1,
exactly as the macOS branch already did.

The death point only looked random because the run order varied.

~~ Both: llvmpipe cannot compile one of Skia's shaders ~~

Mesa's LLVM shader JIT segfaults inside LLVMTypeOf, under
GrGLOpsRenderPass::onDraw, building the fragment shader Skia generates for a
runtime blender. Reproduced on two independent stacks — Mesa 25.2 with LLVM 20
on Linux, and 26.1 with LLVM 22 on Windows — so both legs pin softpipe, the
non-JIT gallium rasterizer, which runs the identical tests green on both and
caps at GL 3.3, well past the 3.0 Ganesh needs. Filed as #4604.

Ruled out along the way, so nobody re-treads it: thread parallelism
(--parallel none --max-threads 1 crashes identically), managed thread stack size
at 2, 16 and 64 MB, LP_NUM_THREADS of 0 and 1, file-descriptor limits at 256,
1024 and 65536, and GL context churn — 400 create/use/destroy cycles are fine.

~~ Supporting changes ~~

  * every class that creates a GPU context joins the existing
    GpuRenderingCollection, mirroring VulkanGpuRenderingCollection. This is what
    #4590 and #4591 asked for; it was not the crash fix, but concurrent GPU
    context use is a real hazard worth closing. Where only a nested class does
    GPU work (SKBlenderTest, SKRuntimeEffectTest) only that class joins, so its
    raster sibling stays parallel — roughly 300 of 6100 tests are serialized
  * GlxContext shares one X11 connection for the process instead of opening and
    closing one per test. That is the leak XCloseDisplay was added for in #4575,
    fixed at the source: one connection instead of 128 and counting, and no
    closing a display while a context minted from it is still current
  * XInitThreads runs before any other Xlib call
  * ganesh-gl.windows and ganesh-gl.linux goldens are harvested and committed,
    since a backend that renders for the first time is unseeded and fails until
    they exist

~~ Result ~~

  * Windows (.NET Framework, x64) — 7415 tests, 0 failed, 23 skipped
  * Windows (.NET Framework, x86) — 7415 tests, 0 failed, 25 skipped
  * Windows (.NET Core)           — 6117 tests, 0 failed, 31 skipped
  * Linux                         — 6117 tests, 0 failed, 34 skipped

Linux previously exited 7 and published nothing at all. Measured locally, GL on
versus off is 6079 against 5910 passing: 169 tests that had never run once.

4575.title: [tests] Make GPU tests required; skip only when declared
4575.body:
[tests] Make GPU tests required; skip only when declared (#4575)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4575
Context: documentation/dev/gpu-test-policy.md

GPU tests brought a backend up inside a try/catch and called Assert.Skip on any
exception. That made "this agent has no GPU" and "this binding is broken"
indistinguishable, and reported both as green. The committed goldens recorded
what it cost: ganesh-gl had a golden for macOS only, and graphite-dawn had none
at all, so those backends had been skipping everywhere for as long as they had
existed. Nobody could answer which backends actually ran.

Invert the default. A backend is now required on every platform listed in
GpuPolicy.RequiredOn, which mirrors the gn args in native/*/build.cake, and a
skip has to be declared. Failing to bring a required backend up is a test
failure, so RendererUnavailableException is deleted along with every catch that
swallowed it.

Skips come from exactly two places, kept separate because that distinction is
what a reader needs when a test skips:

  * the compiled-in table is a statement about a platform — Metal is not
    required off Apple because we do not build it there
  * SKIASHARP_TEST_SKIP_GPU is a statement about one agent, declared per leg in
    scripts/azure-templates-stages-test.yml with its reason and tracking issue
    inline, so it can be removed when that agent gains the capability without
    touching the policy or the documentation

Device and browser hosts never see the agent environment, so the same list
reaches them through the SkiaSharpTestSkipGpu MSBuild property baked into
runtimeconfig.json. An unrecognised backend id is an error, so a typo cannot
quietly leave a backend required.

~~ Latent bugs the required tests surfaced ~~

Five real bugs, every one of them previously invisible as a skip:

  * DllImport used the unversioned libGL and libX11 SONAMEs, which are linker
    symlinks shipped only in -dev packages. Linux GL could never load, and
    every GL test skipped silently for as long as that binding existed.
  * GlxContext.Destroy never called XCloseDisplay — the binding was not even
    declared — leaking an X11 connection per GPU test.
  * SKBlenderTest asserted exact colour equality across two GPU shader paths.
    llvmpipe returns #ff5e0000 where the other path returns #ff5d0000. Raster
    stays exact; the GPU subclass allows a tolerance of one.
  * The Windows software Vulkan ICD was staged for win-x64 only, so x86 had no
    loader and 21 of 25 Vulkan tests failed.
  * Win32VkContext built a Vulkan 1.0 instance and set no MaxAPIVersion, so
    GRContext.CreateVulkan returned null and the test reported an
    ArgumentNullException three frames from the real problem. Skia has required
    1.1 unconditionally since m139 [0] and acquires the core 1.1 device procs
    with no version gate; vkGetDeviceProcAddr gates those on the instance's
    apiVersion, so all nine came back null. It passed against CI's SwiftShader,
    which reports device 1.3.0, and failed on an AMD device reporting 1.4.329 —
    the result depended on the agent's driver.

~~ Limits that are declared, not fixed ~~

Fourteen opt-outs remain, each naming its cause. This is not a regression —
every one was already skipping silently — but they are now enumerable, and
#4591 tracks closing them.

  * Metal is unusable on all three Apple hosts, for three unrelated reasons:
    virtualized Metal hangs the macOS host on shutdown (#4598), Mac Catalyst
    never sees the Mac2 GPU family (#4599), and the iOS simulator cannot
    compile Graphite's gradient pipeline (#4555)
  * Linux GL crashes the host once GLX loads, exiting 7 after 523, 312, 5068
    and 0 tests with zero test failures and no TRX published. The XCloseDisplay
    fix above did not resolve it (#4590)
  * the headless browser the runner launches exposes no WebGPU adapter and the
    runner has no flag passthrough; reported upstream

~~ Structural fallout ~~

The .NET Framework leg is now two jobs. SwiftShader's LLVM JIT cannot resolve
__chkstk in a 32-bit process, so software Vulkan crashes the host on x86 while
x64 runs the same suite green. GpuPolicy models the OS but not the
architecture, so separate jobs are what let x86 opt out while x64 keeps Vulkan
required, and any future x64/x86 divergence becomes visible on its own leg.

Mac Catalyst also stops being non-gating. It carried the repo's only
continueOnError: true, added in #3247, which is the same failure mode this
change exists to remove.

~~ Filed from the Vulkan investigation ~~

  * #4600 — MaxAPIVersion's default of 0 makes Skia trust the loader's version
    rather than the instance's. Worse, since m140 [1] the minimum-version check
    is SK_ABORT rather than a graceful null, so a consumer who correctly
    declares Vulkan 1.0 now aborts the process instead of being able to fall
    back to raster.
  * #4601 — fDeviceLostProc and fDeviceLostContext are not exposed, so
    consumers get no notification on VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST.

4603.title: docs: note the Vulkan 1.1 Ganesh requirement in the 4.148.0 notes sidecar
4603.body:
Skia made Vulkan 1.1 the Ganesh minimum in m139 (0a3150b03b, "[vulkan] Require
Vulkan 1.1 in Ganesh") and promoted the minimum-version check from a debug check
to a fatal SK_ABORT in m140 (dfea59a30f). The consequence is severe and was
undocumented on our side: code that previously got a graceful null back from
GRContext.CreateVulkan on a Vulkan 1.0 instance or device -- and could fall back
to raster -- now aborts the process. It is not an exception, so managed code can
neither catch nor pre-empt it.

Callers are exposed if the VkInstance was created with VkApplicationInfo
.apiVersion below VK_API_VERSION_1_1 (including leaving it at 0, which the Vulkan
spec treats as 1.0), or if GRVkBackendContext.MaxAPIVersion is left at its
default 0. That default makes Skia fall back to vkEnumerateInstanceVersion -- the
loader's version, not the version the instance was actually created with -- so it
can over-declare and ask for entry points the instance cannot serve. The fix is
both halves: declare at least 1.1 on the instance AND set MaxAPIVersion to match.

4.148.0 is the right page, not 4.151.0. Determined from the externals/skia SHA
each release tag actually pins, and whether the two upstream commits are in its
history:

  v3.119.4              7dbfc07d  diverged from both (VulkanUtilsPriv.cpp absent)
  v4.147.0-preview.1.1  6f8139ad  ahead of both (SK_ABORT present)
  v4.148.0              1a155bae  ahead of both (SK_ABORT present)

So the abort first ships in a 4.147.0 preview -- but 4.147.0 has only
-preview.{1,2,3} tags and no v4.147.0, matching its release data (status:
preview, superseded_by 4.148.0, "never released as stable"). v4.148.0 is the
first stable tag, so it is where someone upgrading from 3.119.x meets this. It is
also already the home for this class of change: the sidecar scopes itself to the
v4 breaking changes from the m132/m147 upgrade that no signature diff can show,
and already documents the GRVkBackendContextNative field removals. The new entry
leads that Vulkan group and cross-references it -- that entry covers fields that
disappeared (including fMinAPIVersion), this one covers the surviving
fMaxAPIVersion whose default is now unsafe.

Sidecar only, per spec section 3.7: this file is maintainer-owned and never
machine-written, and editing it flips its sha256 in data.json on the next Prepare
run, which drops the stale prose.json and re-polishes exactly this page. So the
rendered 4.148.0.md, its prose.json and the data.json hash are deliberately left
to CI rather than hand-written here.

Related to #4600

windowsSdkVersion argument, 10.0.22621.0, which matches the AzDO agents.
The hosted runner is windows-2025-vs2026 and ships only Windows SDK
10.0.26100.0, and vcvarsall hard-fails on an SDK that is not installed:

    [ERROR:winsdk.bat] Windows SDK 10.0.22621.0 :
    'C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\include\10.0.22621.0\um'
    not found or was incomplete

Nothing needed that default. Before the MSVC environment was initialized
explicitly there was no such argument at all: gn resolved win_sdk_version
itself and the toolchain interpolated that resolved value into the
vcvarsall command it generated, so the version was always one that
existed on the machine and the two could never disagree. Hardcoding a
constant only meant the build broke wherever that exact SDK was absent -
this runner today, and equally a developer box carrying just a newer one.

Default the argument to empty and omit it from both gn and vcvarsall when
unset, so each detects an SDK that is present. Setting it still pins both
together, so --windowsSdkVersion remains available to build against a
specific SDK.

  * drop the `>nul` that hid the failure. It suppressed the vcvarsall
    banner, but `>nul` redirects only stdout and VsDevCmd writes its
    errors there too, so it discarded the diagnosis along with the
    banner - rerunning with `2>nul` still prints the [ERROR:winsdk.bat]
    lines, while `>nul` yields nothing but the exit code. The banner is
    five lines per architecture and worth keeping in the log.
  * this went unnoticed because benchmark-source runs on pull requests
    only and is skipped on main, so #4570 merged green without the path
    ever being exercised.
  * whether the vcvarsall call is needed at all is left open in #4589:
    every tool is invoked by absolute path and gn emits the SDK include
    and lib directories as explicit -imsvc and /LIBPATH: flags, so it may
    be redundant for our LLVM-based configuration.

4545.title: Add backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels to SKImage and SKSurface
4545.body:
Add backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels to SKImage and SKSurface (#4545)

Requires: mono/skia#295
Related: #3968 (Graphite backend)
Docs: mono/SkiaSharp-API-docs#184

GPU-backed surfaces need a way to read pixels back to the CPU, and on some
backends (notably Graphite) the asynchronous rescale-and-read is the *only*
readback path — Skia gates synchronous GPU ReadPixels behind GPU_TEST_UTILS.
The in-flight Graphite PR (#3968) had added this under Graphite-prefixed names,
but the underlying C++ types (SkImage::AsyncReadResult, SkImage::RescaleGamma,
SkImage::RescaleMode) are core and shared by the raster, Ganesh and Graphite
backends — SkSurface merely aliases the SkImage ones. So this lands the feature
generically on main; #3968 can then drop its SKGraphite* copies and consume it.

Add RequestReadPixels overloads on SKImage and SKSurface that deliver the pixels
to an Action<SKImageReadPixelsResult>. Raster reads invoke the callback
synchronously; Ganesh defers until the work is submitted and drained via the new
GRContext.CheckAsyncWorkCompletion(). The result is a non-owning, callback-scoped
view (deliberately not an SKObject — the native pointer is non-ref-counted and
reused); it is invalidated when the callback returns and throws
ObjectDisposedException afterwards. Failure is signalled by a null result, and
there is no state argument (capture it in the closure).

  * SKImageReadPixelsResult: PlaneCount, GetPlaneRowBytes and a raw zero-copy
    GetPlaneData(ReadOnlySpan<byte>), plus copy-out helpers that outlive the
    callback — CopyPlaneTo (tightly packed, bounded), ToArray, ToImage, ToBitmap.
  * SKImageRescaleGamma { Src, Linear } and SKImageRescaleMode { Nearest, Linear,
    RepeatedLinear, RepeatedCubic }. The convenience overload defaults to
    (Src, Nearest) — the least-transform choice, matching what Skia itself forces
    when no rescale is required (SurfaceContext normalises to kSrc/kNearest at 1:1).
  * Bumps externals/skia to the C API (mono/skia#295) and regenerates the
    P/Invoke bindings; the only hand-written generated piece is the fire-once
    DelegateProxies async-read proxy.

Scope is the RGBA (count()==1) read; YUV420/YUVA420 are a clean additive
follow-up, as the result type and accessors are already multi-plane.

Tested by 18 SKAsyncReadPixelsTest cases: per-pixel pattern correctness read from
an offset srcRect, a deterministic padding-strip unit test, destination-size and
invalid-plane-index edge cases, use-after-callback throwing cleanly, and Ganesh
deferred completion (asserting the false -> pump -> true transition where the
backend supports it).

4531.title: Execute Vulkan visual tests on the Windows CI legs via a software ICD
4531.body:
Execute Vulkan visual tests on the Windows CI legs via a software ICD (#4531)

Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4527

Follow-up to #4527, which added the Silk.NET Vulkan test path and enabled the
ganesh-vulkan visual cells on Linux (Mesa lavapipe) and Android (emulator
SwiftShader). Windows already compiled the tests and built libSkiaSharp with
Vulkan, but the headless CI agent ships no Vulkan driver, so every ganesh-vulkan
cell skipped — the backend was built and never exercised.

Provision a software Vulkan ICD on the Windows test agent so those cells render
and golden-compare instead of skipping, mirroring what the Linux leg does with
lavapipe. A pwsh preBuildStep on both Windows test legs (.NET Core and .NET
Framework) runs scripts/infra/native/windows/install-vulkan-icd.ps1, which
downloads and SHA-256-verifies the Khronos loader (vulkan-1.dll) and Google
SwiftShader (vk_swiftshader.dll + vk_swiftshader_icd.json) from pinned, prebuilt
Silk.NET native packages, extracts them under externals/vulkan-icd, registers the
ICD, and puts the loader on PATH.

Register the ICD in HKLM\SOFTWARE\Khronos\Vulkan\Drivers rather than via
VK_ICD_FILENAMES / VK_DRIVER_FILES: the agent runs elevated, and the loader
ignores those environment variables under elevation, reading the driver list only
from the registry. The script fails the leg on any download, checksum, or registry
error instead of silently degrading back to a skip — provisioning can only add
coverage, never hide a regression.

Seed five ganesh-vulkan.windows goldens harvested from the agent's own SwiftShader
renders; cross-implementation pixel differences mean Windows goldens must come from
the Windows ICD, not from Linux/Android. A future driver-driven mismatch reseeds
via scripts/infra/tests/extract-visual-goldens.py, the same flow as the other legs.

CI-only change: no product, binding, or test-project code is touched (+88/-0), so
apps running against real Vulkan drivers are unaffected. Verified on CI — the x64
Windows .NET Core and .NET Framework legs now run SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Tests.Console
with 15 passed / 0 skipped, including all five VulkanVisualTests.RenderMatchesGolden
("ganesh-vulkan") cells, and golden extraction reports 0 mismatch / 0 unseeded. The
32-bit netfx (x86) slice still skips Vulkan (NotExecuted, never failed) because the
provisioned SwiftShader ICD is 64-bit only. Linux and Android provisioning is
unchanged.
